[Getting started]
**You need:** Windows 10 or 11 (64 bit) or Linux (x86 64 bit), a graphics card that supports DirectX 12 or Vulkan, about 7 GB of free space, and a disc image you made from your own Peter Jackson's King Kong Xbox 360 disc (see [Which version you need](#which-version-you-need)).

1. Download the **KingKong-...-windows-x64.zip** file from the [latest release](https://github.com/TekRantGaming/king-kong-recompiled/releases/latest) and unzip it anywhere. On Linux, see [Linux and Steam Deck](#linux-and-steam-deck-experimental).
2. Run **king_kong.exe**. The launcher opens on its first setup.
3. Choose **Select disc image** and pick your King Kong disc image. The launcher checks it, copies the game files (about 6.3 GB) into a `game` folder next to the exe and takes its artwork from them.
4. The graphics are prepared once, with one progress bar. Then setup offers **Auto detect**, the HD texture pack and the PS2 cutscenes, and walks you through the graphics options and button prompts.
5. Press **PLAY**.

The download contains only this port. **No game files are included**: they come from your own disc. Your saves, settings and downloads are all kept inside the King Kong folder, in `userdata`, so you can copy the whole folder to another drive or PC. If you played an earlier version, your data is moved out of `Documents\king_kong` the first time you start this one. The port is also listed on [Quiver Launcher](https://quiverlauncher.com/apps/peter-jackson-s-king-kong-the-official-game-of-the-movie-king-kong-pc-port), where you can see how it runs for other players.

[Installation]
1. Download the archive for your platform from the
   [Releases page](https://github.com/YesterMester/TheSimpsonsGameRecomp/releases). Use the
   `-NoAVX2` package if your CPU predates AVX2 (the standard package then fails to start, on
   Windows with error 0xc0000142).
2. Extract it anywhere.
3. Start the launcher:
   - Linux and Steam Deck: run `Play.sh`.
   - Windows: run `simpsons-launcher.exe`. It is a standalone program and does not need Python.
4. In the **Install** tab, select your Xbox 360 ISO. The launcher extracts and installs the game
   data.
5. Press **Play**.

**Android (preview):** on an ARM64 phone with Android 10 or newer and Vulkan 1.1, download
`TheSimpsonsGame-Recompiled-Android-arm64.apk` from the release and open it, allowing installs
from your browser or file manager when Android asks. The app installs the game from your ISO or
an already extracted folder, and offers later releases itself.

On Steam Deck, use **Add to Steam** in the launcher from Desktop Mode, then find
**The Simpsons Game (Recompiled)** under Steam's **Non-Steam Games** to play from Game Mode.
If this installation is already registered, the button shows its existing Steam name instead
of adding another copy. It reports command errors and keeps Steam running while it starts.

The 0.0.7.0 Linux launcher bundles its native window and opens fullscreen in Game Mode.
Steam Linux Runtime 1.0 is supported. When Steam runs the shell launcher inside Runtime 2,
it starts the native launcher alongside Steam, keeping the game's Steam identity and controller
environment. **Add to Steam** uses a desktop entry for the game's name and donut icon,
handles spaces and special characters in the installation path, and sends sandboxed requests
to the same host as Steam. If Steam opens an Add a Game dialog, finish it in Desktop Mode.

To start the game without the launcher window, for example from your own Steam shortcut, run
`Play.sh --play` on Linux or `simpsons-launcher.exe --play` on Windows. It uses the same settings
as the launcher's Play button.

The launcher can update itself from the **About** tab. Updates replace only the engine and
launcher files. Your settings, saves and mods are kept. If the installed package does not match
your CPU, the launcher offers the right one.

Updating from 0.0.6.5 or earlier takes two steps. That launcher copies only the files its own
source_text.build:
[Building from source]
The game and the ReXGlue SDK are built together in one CMake project. Continuous integration uses
exactly these steps; see `.github/workflows/build.yml` for the full list of Linux packages.

[Linux]
Requirements: Clang 20, CMake 3.25 or newer, Ninja, pkg-config, and the development packages for
GTK 3, Vulkan, X11 and XCB, Wayland, xkbcommon, udev, ALSA, PulseAudio, PipeWire and D-Bus.

```sh
git clone https://github.com/YesterMester/TheSimpsonsGameRecomp.git
cd TheSimpsonsGameRecomp/simpsons
cmake --preset linux-amd64-relwithdebinfo \
      -DREXSDK_DIR="$PWD/../tools/rexglue-sdk" \
      "-DCMAKE_C_FLAGS=-march=x86-64-v3" "-DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS=-march=x86-64-v3"
cmake --build --preset linux-amd64-relwithdebinfo --target simpsons
cd ..

[Windows]
Requirements: LLVM/Clang 20, Visual Studio Build Tools with the "Desktop development with C++"
workload (for the Windows SDK and linker), CMake 3.25 or newer, Ninja and Python 3.

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/YesterMester/TheSimpsonsGameRecomp.git
cd TheSimpsonsGameRecomp\simpsons
cmake --preset win-amd64-relwithdebinfo `
      -DREXSDK_DIR="$PWD/../tools/rexglue-sdk" `
      "-DCMAKE_C_FLAGS=-march=x86-64-v3" "-DCMAKE_CXX_FLAGS=-march=x86-64-v3"
cmake --build --preset win-amd64-relwithdebinfo --target simpsons
cd ..

- A GPU with a current Vulkan driver (Linux) or Direct3D 12 driver (Windows). The experimental
  Direct3D 11 renderer needs feature level 11.0 or newer.
- A controller is recommended.

[Building from source]
The repository contains no game data, so a build needs your own package plus
sibling checkouts of the (patched) recompilers — see
`docs/xenonrecomp-upstream-bugs.md` for the local patches and
`docs/windows-build-setup.md` for the Windows toolchain. The short form
(Linux, after unpacking the game and regenerating `ppc/` per `CLAUDE.md`):

```
python3 tools/gen_import_stubs.py
cmake -S runtime -B runtime/build -G Ninja
cmake --build runtime/build -j$(nproc)
./runtime/build/cz_runtime --smoke
```

CI (`.github/workflows/build.yml`) builds the host runtime on both platforms
on every push — it proves the host code compiles; it cannot run the game.
macOS is built on the Mac itself (`docs/macos-build-setup.md`,
`tools/release_package_macos.sh`).

[Building from source]
The repository contains no game data, so a build needs your own package plus
sibling checkouts of the (patched) recompilers — the local patches are vendored
in `tools/ci/`, and the Windows toolchain is documented in the sibling port's
[windows-build-setup.md](https://github.com/wivi514/Dead_Rising_2_Case_Zero_Xenon_Recomp/blob/master/docs/windows-build-setup.md).
The short form (Linux, after unpacking the game and regenerating `ppc/` per
`CLAUDE.md`):

```
cmake -S runtime -B runtime/build -G Ninja
cmake --build runtime/build -j$(nproc)
./runtime/build/cw_runtime --smoke
```

CI (`.github/workflows/build.yml`) builds the host runtime on both platforms
on every push — it proves the host code compiles; it cannot run the game.

### What you need

- **Your copy of the game at the supported version:** program `0400486024DEC000`, update v131072, build `e0f3ccfa`.
  Other versions do not work. A `.nup` file, a `.nx` file made from one
  ([NXFormat](https://github.com/fab918/nxformat)'s `nxconvert pack-nup`), or the `romfs` and `exefs` folders.
- 64-bit Windows 10 or 11, or 64-bit Linux with glibc 2.35 or newer (Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12, Fedora, Arch,
  SteamOS ...) and a CPU with AVX2. The Linux AppImage needs AVX2; on Windows, and in a build from source, a CPU
  without it gets a game built for what it has, a little slower.
- A graphics card with Vulkan 1.3 and mesh shaders, with an up-to-date driver: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 20 series or newer,
  AMD Radeon RX 6000 series or newer, or Intel Arc. On Linux, Mesa or NVIDIA's driver. Cards without mesh shaders are
  not supported.
- 8 GB of video memory (VRAM) or more is recommended. Cards with less can use the in-game menu's lower Quality presets.
- 16 GB of RAM or more. A run uses about 10 GB.
- About 60 GB free while building, on an SSD if you can: a hard drive makes the build much slower. You can build on one
  anyway; the builder says so first.
- An internet connection for the download. Nothing else to install: the builder brings its own compiler and tools.
source_text.installation:
### On Windows

For a portable install on an external SSD, run the downloaded setup with `--portable`; see
[Portable Hookshot Builder](docs/windows-portable-builder.md) for folder, move and repair behavior.

1. Open the [latest release](https://github.com/ZuanCrisp/Zelda-OOT-Port/releases/latest) and download `HookshotBuilder.exe`.
2. Run it. It downloads the rest of Hookshot Builder (about 500 MB), checks it, and opens it.
3. Pick your game. The builder looks for `.nup` and `.nx` files in your Downloads, Desktop and Documents folders and lists them
   under **Found on this PC**. Not listed? Press **Browse…**, drop the file on the window, or choose
   **romfs and exefs folders**. The builder checks that it is the right version.
4. Under **Install the game to**, keep the folder (`Games\Hookshot` in your user folder) or press **Change**. Choose
   the **Game language**.
5. Press **Build the game**. It takes about 10 to 45 minutes, depending on your CPU and memory. You can use your PC in
   the meantime.
6. When it says **Your game is ready**, press **Play**. The **Desktop shortcut** and **Start menu entry** boxes are
   ticked: untick them if you don't want them.

Next time, start the game from the Hookshot shortcut, or `hookshot.exe` in the game folder. That is the launcher: it
has **Play**, and **Update** when a newer release is out.

The first start prepares the game's shaders, which takes a while. Later starts are faster.
source_text.build:
## Build from source

For developers, and for players who prefer the command line. The builder windows run the same script,
`nx2/make_game.py`. [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) has more.

<details>
<summary>Windows, from the command line</summary>

```powershell
python -I nx2/make_game.py --nup "C:\path\your-game.nup" --out "C:\Games\Hookshot" --language en-US
python -I nx2/make_game.py --romfs "C:\path\romfs" --exefs "C:\path\exefs" --out "C:\Games\Hookshot" --language en-US
```

Add `--check` with your `.nup` or `--exefs` to only check the game's version. It builds nothing.
Add `--log "C:\path\build.log"` to also save the build's output to a file (UTF-8, replaced if it exists); it works
with `--check` and `--update` too, and on Linux.
`HOOKSHOT_JOBS=<n>` (or `--jobs <n>`) limits how many files compile at once.
`HOOKSHOT_MEM_LIMIT_GB=<n>` lets the compilers take that many GB together, whatever is free now; up to 4 always run.

You need:

- Python 3 from python.org (the Microsoft Store's Python installs packages where `python -I` does not look), with
  `pip install -r requirements.txt` (core tools plus the button-prompt packages).
- [llvm-mingw](https://github.com/mstorsjo/llvm-mingw) (the `ucrt-x86_64` build), unpacked as `llvm-mingw` in the
  clone or with `HOOKSHOT_MINGW` set to its folder. Without it the build uses the clang from
  [emsdk](https://github.com/emscripten-core/emsdk) at `C:\emsdk` with Visual Studio's C++ tools and the Windows SDK
  (`HOOKSHOT_MSVC=1` forces that route).
- What the builder's `tools` folder carries and a clone does not. Run `HookshotBuilder.exe` once: the folder is
  `%LOCALAPPDATA%\HookshotBuilder\versions\<version>\HookshotBuilder\tools`. The builder sets the variables itself;
  from the command line, set them before you run `make_game.py`:
  - `tools\cpm`: the Vulkan headers and FFmpeg. Set `RX_CPM` to this folder. Without it (and without system
    Vulkan / SPIR-V / VMA headers or `HOOKSHOT_*_HEADERS`), the standalone build stops instead of shipping a
    game with no renderer.
  - `tools\wgpu-native`: set `WGPU_NATIVE` to this folder.
  - `tools\third_party`: the prebuilt files a clone lacks (`a64emit`, `lld-link`, `zbic` and SDL2). Copy its `.dll`,
    `.exe`, `.lib` and `.sha1` files to the same places under `third_party\`.
  - `tools\work`: copy it to `work\`. It holds the hot-function list, the link order, the profile and the icon;
    without them the game builds but runs slower.

source_text.general:
## Project status

Experimental. Players have reported on many PCs, from Kokiri Forest to the dungeons: the table says what works and
what does not yet. Open problems are collected in tracking issues, linked below.

| What | Status |
|---|---|
| Kokiri Forest: reaching gameplay and walking around | ✅ Works |
| Sound, controller, keyboard and saves | ✅ Works |
| In-game menu, frame generation and upscaling | ✅ Works |
| Flicker (the picture flashing too bright while moving) | ✅ Fixed in v2.0.2 (#645) |
| Ground fog vanishing when looking down | ✅ Fixed in v2.0.2 (#638) |
| Models with missing pieces (doors, fences, parts of trees) | ✅ Fixed where tested, more play needed |
| Stutter when entering new areas | ⚠️ Still happens the first time you visit a place. The next visits are smooth |
| Performance | ⚠️ Depends on the PC: some reach a steady 60 fps, others stay below it, more so in Hyrule Field |
| Hyrule Field, Castle Town, Kakariko and the dungeons | ⚠️ Players got there, with open bugs: lighting and shadows (#1004), crashes and freezes (#2507) |
| Ultrawide and 4:3 | ✅ Works. The Aspect ratio row's default, Monitor's shape, widens the 3D to the screen ([#2119](https://github.com/ZuanCrisp/Zelda-OOT-Port/commit/145eed2650d9d2cebad85a8a0052d302086015c7)); the HUD keeps its 16:9 size with its corners at the screen's edges, or in the middle 16:9 with the HUD layout row; movies stay in the middle 16:9 |
| NVIDIA cards | ✅ Works. The most tested |
| AMD cards | ⚠️ Many tested: reports from the RX 6600, RX 6800 XT, RX 7800 XT, RX 7900 XTX and RX 9070 XT. On Windows, the RX 6000 cards (Navi 21 and 22) draw task and mesh shaders through the compute fallback by default, as the driver lost the GPU with them (#1747, [#1992](https://github.com/ZuanCrisp/Zelda-OOT-Port/commit/1396428d0bfcde68b5c7bd63f9837564d9af1a05), [#2215](https://github.com/ZuanCrisp/Zelda-OOT-Port/commit/f95d80f5371821420c5a47a0c7e9f73e7f484abc)). Driver crashes and device lost are still reported ([#996](https://github.com/ZuanCrisp/Zelda-OOT-Port/commit/f95d80f5371821420c5a47a0c7e9f73e7f484abc)) |
| Intel cards | ❓ Few reports, many of them black screens or crashes (#999) |
[trecho abreviado]

source_text.system:
### Download and use

1. Download `SotC-PC.zip` from [Releases](../../releases) and unzip it into a folder.
2. Run **`SotC.exe`**. On first start the launcher searches the PC's drives for:
   - the game folder (the CUSA08809 or CUSA08034 dump with `eboot.bin`, `sce_module` and `sce_sys`);
   - the sound modules (`libSceNgs2.sprx` and `libSceUlt.sprx`) of an installed shadPS4
     (`user/sys_modules`), which it copies to the port's data folder;
   - a shadPS4 save of the game, which it offers to import;
   - the game's DLCs, if any (shadPS4's `addcont` folder, or a folder with one subfolder per DLC).
3. Check the **Game and saves** page. The **game library** works like shadPS4's.
4. Click **PLAY**.

Requirements: Windows 10/11 64-bit and a **Vulkan 1.3** GPU (NVIDIA, AMD or Intel with a recent
driver). No Python install needed. **The game folder should be on an SSD** (NVMe best): on a hard
disk new areas stutter much more.

| What | Where from | What for |
|---|---|---|
| CUSA08809 (EU 1.01) or CUSA08034 (US 1.00) game dump | your PS4, through GoldHEN | the game |
| decrypted `libSceNgs2.sprx`, `libSceUlt.sprx` (optional) | your PS4 (`/system/common/lib/`, GoldHEN FTP), or shadPS4's `user/sys_modules` | the firmware's sound mixer (since v0.75 the port's built-in mixer plays the sound without them) |

The patch modes (60 FPS, 16x filtering) apply to EU 1.01 and US 1.00 (the same executable);
other versions run at 30 FPS. Each release keeps its own saves (`user/savedata/1/<title ID>`),
and only DLC of the same region is used.

other versions run at 30 FPS. Each release keeps its own saves (`user/savedata/1/<title ID>`),
and only DLC of the same region is used.

source_text.general:
### Known issues

- The first start after updating rebuilds the shaders: the first load is slow and stutters.
- **Texture quality "Maximum"** can close the game in very wide views (sword raised against the
  sun, the last colossus' area; #186). In PS4 Pro mode it is experimental since 0.60.6-C1 (with
  tabnul's page allocator fix): an hour without a crash in our test, but some colour garbage can
  still show in the 7th and 8th colossus' areas after several visits.
- **Frame generation (FSR 3) with DLSS:** text and HUD may shake; best left off.
- The first start after an update rebuilds the GPU driver's shader cache: about 2 minutes of
  loading screen, and short stalls the first time each area is visited.
- **AMD GCN** cards (RX 470–590, Vega, APUs on the legacy driver): characters and Agro may glow
  white (#152, #158, #187). 0.60.5 adds the LDS barriers these cards were missing (PR #205), which
  is the likely fix: please report whether it helps. `SOTC_AMD64_LDS=0` turns it off.
- **60 FPS:** since 0.60 the game targets 60 FPS itself (its PS4 Pro Performance mode), which
  should fix the 60 FPS physics (the 2nd colossus' wall, colossi "flying"); still being tested
  there. `SOTC_MODES=af16` in the extra variables goes back to the old mode.
- **Frame generation** (experimental): the health/stamina bars may shake (`SOTC_FG_HUDLESS=1`
  tries a HUD-less image), and it only matters at 30 FPS.
- With 8 GB of video memory or less, pick a lower **Video memory use** level if the game runs out.

## Get started

**You need:** your own game files (see [Game files](docs/game-files.md)), Windows 10 or later or Linux on x86-64, a
GPU with Vulkan 1.3, 16 GB of RAM, a CPU with SSE4.2 (AVX2 runs faster) and about 20 GB of free disk space.

1. Download the latest build from [Releases](https://github.com/Revivedx/SavageWindRecomp/releases/latest):
   - **Windows:** the file ending in `windows.zip`. Extract it to a folder you can write to, not Program Files.
   - **Linux and Steam Deck:** the file ending in `x86_64.AppImage`. Make it executable and run it
     ([docs/linux.md](docs/linux.md)).
   - **Linux on ARM:** the file ending in `aarch64.AppImage`. It is highly experimental.
2. Start it and choose the folder with your extracted game (`exefs/` and `romfs/`). Then choose **Set up game files**.
   It checks the version, copies the files and recompiles the game code once, about 15 minutes on a 12-thread CPU.
   Your own files aren't changed.
3. Play. Settings and languages are in the game's Options. **Savage Wind Configuration** has your game files and the
   rest of the settings.

**Updating:** from version 0.5.1 on, Savage Wind Configuration updates it in one click, on Windows and in the Linux
AppImages. Before that, extract the new zip over the old folder or use the new AppImage. Your game files, saves and
settings stay.

Something wrong? See the [FAQ](docs/FAQ.md), which also lists the known issues.

## Installing

### Windows

Requirements: Windows 10 or later, an x86-64 CPU with SSE4.2 (AVX2/FMA machines get a faster build), a GPU with Vulkan 1.3 and `VK_EXT_external_memory_host`, about 36 GiB free during setup (20 GiB after).

1. Download `TotK-Setup-<version>-windows.zip` from [Releases](../../releases/latest) and unpack it.
2. Start `TotK-Setup.exe`. If SmartScreen warns about an unsigned app, choose *More info*, then *Run anyway*.
3. Pick your game files, the language and an install folder, and press *Start*. The setup builds the game once. With
   an NVIDIA RTX GPU it also downloads NVIDIA DLSS, unless you untick *Download NVIDIA DLSS*; turn DLSS on in the
   menu (F1).
4. Play `totk.exe` from the install folder.

### Linux

Requirements: as on Windows, plus Linux 6.7 or later and glibc 2.34 or later (Ubuntu 22.04, Debian 12, Fedora 35, SteamOS 3).

1. Download `TotK-Setup-x86_64.AppImage` from [Releases](../../releases/latest), or build it ([docs/installer.md](docs/installer.md), "Linux release").
2. Make it executable (`chmod +x TotK-Setup-x86_64.AppImage`) and start it. On a Steam Deck, do this in Desktop Mode.
3. Pick your game files, the language and an install folder, and press *Start*.
4. Play `totk` from the install folder.

To update, run a newer setup on the same folder; saves and settings are kept. Settings are in the in-game menu and in `totk.ini` ([totk.ini.example](totk.ini.example) lists every key). Controls: [docs/controls.md](docs/controls.md).

## Requirements

- **Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit**, and a **processor with SSE4.1** (Intel Core i3/i5/i7, AMD FX or newer).
- **A graphics card with Vulkan 1.2** and current drivers for CoreGS 2.0 (GSdx can also use Direct3D 11 on older cards).
- **Your own disc image** of Gran Turismo 4 USA v2.00 (SCUS-97328), and of Spec II 1.10 for the mod, as a plain `.iso`.
  The launcher reads the image where you keep it; it is not copied.

The launcher checks the processor and the graphics card before setup and before Play, and says what is missing.
source_text.installation:
## Install

1. Download the installer (**`GT4Recomp-Setup-<version>.exe`**) or the portable zip from
   [Releases](https://github.com/moesuito/gt4-staticrecomp/releases): the latest release for Stable, or the newest
   pre-release for Beta.
2. Start **GT4Recomp** and choose your disc image. The launcher checks it, prepares the game and its shaders.
3. Press **Play**.

Updates install from the launcher. Your settings, saves and replays are kept per Windows user in `%APPDATA%\GT4Recomp`
(the portable build keeps them in its own folder). Building from source needs your own game files and a development
environment: see the [Build guide](docs/BUILD.md).

### Controls

Controllers work out of the box with the DualShock 2 layout (analog triggers with pressure for throttle and brake) and
can be remapped in the launcher (Settings > Controls). The keyboard has a fixed layout:

| Key | Action (PS2 button) |
|---|---|
| W · Enter | Accelerate, confirm (Cross) |
| S | Brake (Square) |
| Space | Handbrake (Circle) |
| A · D · arrow keys | Steer, navigate (D-pad) |
| Backspace · Esc | Back (Triangle) |
| Shift | Nitro (R1) |
| R · F | Gear up · gear down (R2 · L2) |
| Q | Look back (L1) |
| C · Tab | Camera (Select) |
| P | Start / Pause |
| Alt+Enter, F11 | Borderless fullscreen |
source_text.build:
## How it works

The EE game code is translated ahead of time into C++ and compiled for x86-64. The VU1 microcode, stored encrypted
inside the executable, is recovered and compiled offline and verified against a reference interpreter; the VU0
microprograms are compiled the same way. IOP system services are native, and frames are paced by one high-resolution
clock. This is a **hybrid recompilation**: PS2 hardware is still modelled in software, so we do not claim zero emulation
or full PS2 fidelity. Details: [Architecture](docs/ARCHITECTURE.md).
source_text.general:
## Known issues

- **Busy driving views on laptop processors (CoreGS 2.0):** the player's view with the HUD and the rear-view mirror can
  drop below 60 FPS on mid-range laptops (the first license, some city tracks). The cause is known (palette changes split
  the drawing into too many batches) and the fix is planned for the next release candidate.
- **Photo mode on slower graphics cards (CoreGS 2.0):** frame times can be uneven.
- **Some AMD Radeon RX 5000/6000 drivers closed the game while CoreGS 2.0 prepared its shaders.** 1.3.0-rc14 guards
  against it; GSdx works on those PCs.
- **Some license demos and menu backgrounds do not play**; every license test is playable
  ([why](docs/LICENSE-DEMO-CIPHER.md)).
- **Spec II:** only images with Spec II 1.10's game code are supported; earlier Spec II releases are refused.
- Menus, movies and photo mode stay 16:9 (pillarboxed) at other aspect ratios.
- The installer is not code-signed: Windows SmartScreen may warn on the first start ("More info", "Run anyway").
- Most testing was on an AMD graphics card; NVIDIA and Intel cards have had less testing.

source_text.system: ## 🧰 Requirements - **Windows:** Windows 10 or 11 (x64) and a Direct3D 12 graphics card. The compiler is the [standalone tools](#no-visual-studio) (what the installer fetches), or a Visual Studio 2022 you already have with *Desktop development with C++*, *C++ Clang tools for Windows* and a Windows SDK. - **Linux (experimental):** an x86-64 distribution with FFmpeg 6.1 or newer (such as Ubuntu 24.04 or Linux Mint 22), and a Vulkan-compatible GPU with a Vulkan driver. Follow the [Linux setup](#linux) to install build dependencies and prepare the game. - An AVX2-capable CPU and 16 GB of RAM for the first build. - Git and Python are not needed: `setup.ps1` fetches the port's own copies into `tools\git` (MinGit, only when the PC has no Git) and `tools\python` (python.org's 3.11.9, 17 MB) and runs every tool on them; nothing is installed in Windows. - About 25 GB free on Windows or 30 GB on Linux, including about 17 GB of game files. - Your own GT5 disc (BCES00569, BCUS98114 or BCAS20108) and the means to dump it, and [RPCS3](https://rpcs3.net/download) to install PS3 firmware and decrypt the game's executable. ### A processor that calculates wrongly The game is built on your PC by long calculations, and they assume every processor gives the right answer. On some PCs one or two logical processors don't (seen on a 14th generation Intel desktop processor: two of its 28 failed a fixed job most of the time, the other 26 never). The signs are tools stopping with errors that make no sense, compiler crashes, or a game that misbehaves. Setup checks for this before it generates and builds the game: a small fixed job runs on every processor, and any processor that gives an error or a different result is left out of the whole install. You are told which. The result is kept for 30 days in `.gt5\pc-check.json`. To run the check by hand: ``` powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File pc-check.ps1 ``` Leaving processors out gets the game built, but the PC still has the fault, and other programs (and the game itself) can hit it. What usually cures it: the newest BIOS for your motherboard (for Intel 13th and 14th generation processors it carries Intel's fix), the processor maker's default settings in the BIOS instead of the motherboard's "performance" ones, memory at its standard speed, and current drivers. ### No Visual Studio needed `GT5-Installer.bat` never installs or changes Visual Studio. When the PC has no Visual Studio with the Clang tools and a Windows SDK, it runs `get-toolchain.ps1`, which puts the same compiler tools in the install folder (`tools\toolchain`). By hand, the script puts them in one folder you choose, on any drive. In the `gt5-recomp` folder, in PowerShell: ``` powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File get-toolchain.ps1 ``` - It suggests a `toolchain` folder next to `gt5-recomp`. Type another folder to put it somewhere else, for example on a second drive. [trecho original abreviado]
source_text.installation: ## ⬇️ Install **The easy way, on Windows 10 or 11:** 1. Download **[GT5-Installer.bat](https://github.com/MormonFTP-hub/gt5-recomp/releases/latest/download/GT5-Installer.bat)** and double-click it. If Windows warns about a downloaded file, choose **Run** (or **More info**, then **Run anyway**). 2. In its window, pick two things and press **Install**: - **your GT5 game**: the folder of your disc dump (the one with `PS3_GAME` in it) or an `.iso`; - **PS3UPDAT.PUP**, Sony's free PS3 system software (the window has a button that opens Sony's page). That's all, and it all happens in that one window: the steps, a progress bar, and what went wrong if something does. Nothing is installed into Windows. It downloads this code and, into the install folder, its own copies of Git (38 MB, only when the PC has none), Python (17 MB) and the compiler tools (about 1.5 GB, into the install folder: **no Visual Studio is installed or changed**), unlocks your game's executable and the system software (with the port's own small tool; RPCS3 is fetched only if that fails, as a tool: the game itself runs natively as `gt5.exe`, not in an emulator), builds the game (about an hour the first time) with both renderers (DirectX 12 and Vulkan), adds AMD FSR 3 frame generation and, on a PC with an NVIDIA RTX card, NVIDIA DLSS, and puts **Gran Turismo 5 (PC)** on your desktop, which opens the [launcher](#launcher). Nothing from the game is ever uploaded or shared. Some of what it downloads comes under another company's licence (Microsoft's C++ libraries in the compiler tools, when it fetches those; NVIDIA DLSS): the line by the **Install** button names them, with links, and pressing Install accepts them. Rather do it by hand? See [Setup](#setup). On Linux? See [Linux](#linux).
source_text.build: ### No Visual Studio needed `GT5-Installer.bat` never installs or changes Visual Studio. When the PC has no Visual Studio with the Clang tools and a Windows SDK, it runs `get-toolchain.ps1`, which puts the same compiler tools in the install folder (`tools\toolchain`). By hand, the script puts them in one folder you choose, on any drive. In the `gt5-recomp` folder, in PowerShell: ``` powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File get-toolchain.ps1 ``` - It suggests a `toolchain` folder next to `gt5-recomp`. Type another folder to put it somewhere else, for example on a second drive. - It downloads about 1.5 GB and keeps about 1.5 GB: LLVM 19.1.5 (clang-cl), CMake and Ninja from their official GitHub pages, and Microsoft's C++ libraries and Windows SDK, fetched from Microsoft by [mmozeiko's portable-msvc.py](https://gist.github.com/mmozeiko). Every download is checked. - Microsoft's part comes under Microsoft's licence. The script shows you the link and only goes on when you type `yes`. - No administrator rights, and nothing is installed into Windows. To remove the tools, delete the folder. Then run `setup.ps1` as usual (it also offers to run `get-toolchain.ps1` when it finds no Visual Studio). When there's no Visual Studio, the build uses these tools.

source_text.build:
## Building

Most people should use a [release](https://github.com/RyGT-Team/RyGTS/releases). To build it
yourself on Windows you need:

| What | Why | Where |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Git | cloning, with submodules | [git-scm.com](https://git-scm.com/download/win) |
| MSYS2 (UCRT64 shell) with GCC, CMake and Ninja | the runtime libraries (`libs\*.prx`) and the converter | [msys2.org](https://www.msys2.org) |
| Internet access while configuring | CMake downloads FFmpeg's prebuilt libraries once | |
| .NET Framework 4.x (part of Windows 10/11) | the launcher, `RyGTLauncher.exe` | built in |
| Visual Studio's C++ tools with LLVM (clang) | only for GT7's stub library (`runtime/gt7/build.cmd`) | [visualstudio.microsoft.com](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com) |
| Visual Studio 2022 with "C++ Clang tools", the Vulkan SDK | only to rebuild the renderer (`libSceVideoOut.prx`) | [visualstudio.microsoft.com](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com), [vulkan.lunarg.com](https://vulkan.lunarg.com) |

You also need everything a release needs to run: your own decrypted GT Sport dump (CUSA03220,
update 1.69) and/or GT7 dump (CUSA24769), and your PS4 firmware's system modules and fonts.

### 1. Get the code with its submodules

```sh
git clone --recursive -b development https://github.com/mlgprorektm8/RyGT.git
cd RyGT
```

Already cloned without `--recursive`? Run `git submodule update --init --recursive`. Without the
submodules (SDL2, FFmpeg, FreeType, stb, glslang and the others in `3rdparty`), CMake builds only
the converter and **skips every runtime library**, so `GTSport.exe` then fails to load
`libScePad.prx` and the rest. The configure step warns about this.

### 2. Install the compiler (MSYS2)

Open the **MSYS2 UCRT64** shell (not "MSYS2 MSYS") and run:

```sh
pacman -S --needed git mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-gcc mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-cmake mingw-w64-ucrt-x86_64-ninja
```

### 3. Build the runtime libraries and the converter

In the UCRT64 shell, from the RyGT folder:

```sh
cmake -S . -B build/windows-mingw -G Ninja -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release -DRTY_ENABLE_LTO=OFF -DRTY_BUILD_GUI=OFF
cmake --build build/windows-mingw --target libs ryty
```

Check that the configure output has no "3rdparty submodules are missing" warning. The results:

- `build/windows-mingw/core/libs/libs/*.prx`: the runtime libraries. They go in the game folder's
  `libs` folder.
- `build/windows-mingw/core/relinker/ryty.exe`: the converter. It goes in `converter`.

The libraries also need `libgcc_s_seh-1.dll`, `libstdc++-6.dll` and `libwinpthread-1.dll` from
`C:\msys64\ucrt64\bin` next to `GTSport.exe` and `GT7.exe` (a release already has them). The same
libraries serve both games.

Building from PowerShell or cmd instead of the UCRT64 shell? Put `C:\msys64\ucrt64\bin` first on
`PATH`, or the build fails without a clear error.

### 4. Build the launcher

From cmd or PowerShell:

```bat
loader\build.cmd C:\path\to\your\game\folder
```

Fonte histórica — ryGT7 integrado ao RyGT:
## Alpha status

Verified locally: clean-folder conversion and launch to the GT7 main menu, and racing at Deep Forest.
The tested dump reports `APP_VER=01.00` in its metadata. Other updates and hardware are unverified;
folder-selection support does not guarantee that every update converts or plays correctly.
Crashes, rendering errors, and shader compilation stutter remain possible. Online play has been
tested between two players (Australia and the UK, and with a player on Linux): see
[Online play](#online-play) for what works.

This first prerelease fixes crowd instances flickering black or jumping because GPU output ranges
overlapped, and black streamed textures on Deep Forest's pit building. Validation included 512
shader-lowering checks, GPU captures with no remaining overlapping crowd writes, and 60-frame
crowd recordings without the large black flashes.

The second prerelease adds a fix for flickering night shadows at Yas Marina: cached render targets
are no longer reused after the game remaps their memory, which left an empty shadow map on
alternate frames. Packed-float render targets are also cleared and filled correctly. This fix is
not yet confirmed in game.

The current source also carries the Alsace shadow band and rear-view mirror fixes, the optional
Offline mode patch step in Set up (see the release notes and [the launcher guide](loader/README.md)),
and the racing wheel, ultrawide and frame generation work described in the next section.

The launcher retains display, FSR, optional DLSS, input bindings, controller ports, wheel, shader
compilation, and logging controls. GT Sport-specific script preparation and graphics patches are
removed from its interface. The package ships the DLSS plugin (`dlss\ryGT_dlss.dll`, see
[the plugin's notes](plugins/dlss/README.md)); NVIDIA's DLSS files come from the launcher's download button. AMD FSR is available in the supplied renderer.

## Requirements

- Windows 10/11 x64
- [Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools](https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/downloads/) with the **C++** workload (includes CMake and Ninja)
- [Git](https://git-scm.com/)
- [Python 3](https://www.python.org/) (disc extraction and the native VU1/IOP generators)
- ~20 GB of free space (the extracted disc takes ~8.5 GB); 16 GB of RAM recommended (the build uses every core)
- Your own copy of **God of War (NTSC-U, SCUS-97399)**

`scripts\1_instalar_herramientas.cmd` installs Git and the Build Tools with `winget`.
source_text.installation:
## Building and running

**1. Extract the disc.** As in Waffle565's port, the game reads its data from the extracted disc files,
each at its original sector (the ISO is not read). With Python 3:

```bat
python tools\iso_extract.py "D:\God of War.iso" game --layout
```

This leaves the executable `SCUS_973.99`, the `.IRX` modules, `PART1.PAK`/`PART2.PAK` (both DVD layers) and the
`.disc_layout` index in `game\`. If the ELF is somewhere else, point `GOW_ELF` at it; the disc files must sit next
to it. `scripts\ejecutar.ps1` extracts the disc by itself on first run if it finds `God of War.iso` in the folder
above the ELF's, and `GOW_ISO=<path>` makes the runtime read the image directly.

**2. Install the tools** (first time only):

```bat
scripts\1_instalar_herramientas.cmd
```

**3. Build** (20–40 min the first time):

```bat
scripts\2_compilar.cmd
```

The script clones PS2Recomp into `<drive>:\gowport` (a short path to avoid the 260-character limit;
configurable with `GOW_WORK`), pins commit `c5a9d02`, applies the patches in `patches/`, generates the C++ code and builds
`ps2EntryRunner.exe`. The log is written to `logs\2_compilar.log`.

To build with clang instead of MSVC (about 4 minutes instead of 45–60, with bit-identical VU1 results), download
an LLVM for Windows (`clang+llvm-*-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`) and point `GOW_LLVM` at its `bin` folder before
building: `set GOW_LLVM=C:\llvm\bin`. It builds in `out\build-clang`; Visual Studio is still needed for its headers
and libraries.

With clang the build can also be optimized with a profile of your own play (PGO; the VU1 runs 10–12 % faster in
combat): build with `set GOW_PGO=generar`, play for a while with `scripts\3_ejecutar_manual.cmd` (when you close the window the
profile is left in `<GOW_WORK>\pgo`) and build again with `set GOW_PGO=usar`. The profile never leaves your machine.

Release builds disable function and IOP RPC traces by default. For diagnostics, use
`scripts\2_compilar.cmd -Trazas`. To measure game `vid::Flip` calls separately from window refreshes,
run `powershell -File scripts\probar_rendimiento.ps1`; see [the profiling notes](docs/ESTADO.md#medicion-de-rendimiento-2026-10-05).

**4. Run:**

```bat
scripts\3_ejecutar.cmd          :: 60 seconds, output in logs\
scripts\3_ejecutar_manual.cmd   :: no time limit
```

**F2** shows an FPS meter (also with `GOW_FPS=1`); see [`docs/CONTROLES.md`](docs/CONTROLES.md#medidor-de-fps).
The game starts in borderless fullscreen; **F11** switches to a window and back (`GOW_PANTALLA_COMPLETA=0` starts
windowed). **F1** opens the runtime debugger.
`GOW_PANORAMICO=ampliado` uses the enhanced widescreen (a wider view instead of cropping top and bottom, an idea by
nemesis2000 and CRASHARKI); it draws more and costs performance.
`GOW_ASPECTO=21:9`, `32:9` (or any number, or `auto` for the window's own) sets the picture aspect for ultrawide
screens: the view widens at the sides like the enhanced widescreen; the HUD is stretched.
`GOW_HZ=120` (experimental) lets the game logic run above 60 frames per second (up to 120, depending on the scene and
the computer) and presents up to 120 pictures per second; see [`docs/CONTROLES.md`](docs/CONTROLES.md#120-hz).

**5. Native IOP (optional, as in Waffle565's port).** Compiles the game's 8 IRX modules ahead of time and
shortens loading (gameplay starts at ~21 s instead of ~34 s). One run dumps the modules and the next build
uses them:

```bat
set PS2X_IOP_DUMP_MODULES=%CD%\logs\iop_modulos
scripts\3_ej

## Requirements

- Windows 10/11 64-bit, or Linux x86-64. Windows can use Vulkan or Direct3D 12. Linux uses Vulkan. Vulkan 1.3 is what the Vulkan path asks for.
- About 4 GB of free RAM while playing (the game peaks near 1.1 GB). A build needs more: about 2 GB at 4 jobs, about 3.2 GB at 8. About 15 GB of disk. [`docs/launcher.md`](docs/launcher.md)
- Your own copy of Forza Horizon: a disc image, a Games on Demand package, or an extracted folder. Title Update 4 and DLC are optional. TU4 is what you want for Horizon Rally and the 1000 Club.
- A controller, a keyboard and mouse, or a wheel.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **macOS is a source-build experiment.** The launcher does not support macOS, and there is no Mac download.
> Opening drives render on Apple Silicon. Full races, save reloads and physical controllers still need validation.
> [macOS setup and limits](docs/macos.md)

## Install with the launcher

This is the way to install. The launcher builds the game on your machine from your own files. Nothing of the game is downloaded.

1. Get the launcher from the [latest release](https://github.com/FH1-ReImagined/ForzaHorizon1-ReImagined/releases/latest). On Windows, the installer. On Linux, the Flatpak (recommended on SteamOS) or the `.tar.gz`. From v0.1.9 onward the launcher checks for updates itself (**About > Launcher updates**).
   The Flatpak is `flatpak install --user ForzaHorizon1-ReImagined-x86_64.flatpak`. It pulls the freedesktop SDK runtime from Flathub. Install the compiler extension once, or the launcher downloads a 2 GB compiler instead and tells you so:

   ```sh
   flatpak install flathub org.freedesktop.Sdk.Extension.llvm22//26.08
   ```

   **On SteamOS (Steam Deck):** in Desktop Mode, download the `.flatpak` and open it in Dolphin (Discover installs it) or run the command above, install the compiler extension, then in Steam choose **Games > Add a Non-Steam Game to My Library** and pick **Forza Horizon 1: ReImagined**. It then starts from Game Mode. [`docs/steam_deck.md`](docs/steam_deck.md)

2. In Setup, **Game files**: your disc image, Games on Demand package, or an extracted folder. **Updates & DLC**: Title Update 4 and your DLC folder, if you have them.
3. **Build.** The launcher generates the game from your copy and compiles it. A measured build at 4 jobs on an 8-core PC took about 4.6 minutes ([`docs/launcher.md`](docs/launcher.md)). It can be cancelled and resumed, and it runs again only when something changed.
4. **Prebuild shaders** (optional, Vulkan). This builds pipelines from your own game files before you play, so the first visit to a place stutters less. The launcher offers it again after a driver, launcher or graphics-setting change. [`docs/shader_prebuild.md`](docs/shader_prebuild.md)
5. **Play.** Settings cover display, controls, audio, online, profile and advanced options. **Saves** is the backup and profile editor.

Details: [`docs/launcher.md`](docs/launcher.md).

To verify a download when its release includes `SHA256SUMS`, download that file from the
same release. On Windows, run `certutil -hashfile .\YourDownloadedSetup.exe SHA256` or, in
PowerShell, `Get-FileHash .\YourDownloadedSetup.exe -Algorithm SHA256`, and compare the hash with
the matching filename in `SHA256SUMS` ([details](docs/launcher.md#verify-your-download)).
On Linux, put both files in the same folder and run
`sha256sum --ignore-missing -c SHA256SUMS`. A match confirms the downloaded bytes match
the published checksum; it does not certify that the program is safe or code-signed.

# LAS Recomp

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **This project was made almost exclusively with AI.** Nearly all of the code, tooling, reverse engineering and
> documentation in this repository was written by and will be maintained by an AI (Anthropic's Claude, through Claude Code),
> directed, tested and reviewed by a human. As a huge fan of this game, I made this for myself. Sharing it is a courtesy.
> If you don't agree with the use of AI or don't trust code written by AI, that is your right, but I'm not interested
> in the controversy in relation to this project. You may simply ignore this project and its code.
> As with anything on the internet, you run the code at your own discretion.

**LAS Recomp** is a static recompilation of *The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening* (Nintendo Switch, 2019) into a
native Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iOS application.

> [!NOTE]
> Currently supported platforms:
> - macOS - Apple Silicon only, Metal graphics backend + MetalFX
> - Windows - x86-64 only, Vulkan graphics backend
> - Linux - x86-64, Vulkan graphics backend (AppImage)
> - Android - arm64, Vulkan graphics backend
> - iPhone and iPad - arm64, Metal graphics backend (sideloaded: see [iPhone and iPad](#iphone-and-ipad))
> - Linux aarch64 (ARM) - **experimental**: on the [nightly](https://github.com/peiikai/LASRecomp/releases/tag/nightly) page; reports welcome
>   ([docs/linux.md](docs/linux.md) lists what to include)

## System requirements

These are the minimums during the beta and may change as development continues.

**macOS:** any Apple Silicon Mac (M1 or newer) on macOS 15 or newer. Intel Macs aren't supported.

**Windows and Linux:**

| | Minimum |
|---|---|
| OS | Windows 10 or 11 (64-bit), or 64-bit Linux from about 2022 or newer (including the Steam Deck) |
| CPU | x86-64 with AVX2 and FMA: Intel 4th gen (Haswell) or newer, or AMD Ryzen |
| GPU | Vulkan 1.3 with an up-to-date driver, about as fast as a Switch or faster. For example: NVIDIA GTX 900 series or newer, AMD Rad
source_text.build:
## Building from source

Every platform needs your own game files (v1.0.0, v1.0.1 or v1.1.0): build first, then use the start screen's game-file setup.
`make gen` then recompiles the game code from your own game files into `generated/`, and `make` builds it into its own
library next to the app (`build/lasgame.*`); without it the start screen builds that library itself, as it does for
players. Release builds hold none of the game's code: the start screen builds it on each player's machine from their
own game files, with the bundled generator (`make gen-helper`) and compiler (`tools/fetch_zig.sh`).

### macOS

Requirements: Apple Silicon, Xcode command line tools (clang), [Homebrew](https://brew.sh) `sdl3` and `ffmpeg`,
Python 3.12.

1. Build: `make -j10` -> `build/lasrecomp`. Set up your game files (above), then `make gen` and `make -j10` again.
2. Randomizer: create the Python environment for LAS-Randomizer, from `third_party/LAS-Randomizer`:
   `python3.12 -m venv venv && venv/bin/pip install -r requirements.txt`.
3. Run: `./build/lasrecomp extracted` (start screen) or `./build/lasrecomp extracted --play` (straight into the game).
4. Package: `make deps` (once: SDL3, FFmpeg, keystone and Python from pinned sources, built for macOS 15),
   `make rando-helper` (the seed generator as a standalone helper, so players need no Python), `make gen-helper` and
   `tools/fetch_zig.sh` (what the start screen builds the game code with), then `make app` ->
   `build/LAS Recomp.app` (macOS 15+, Apple Silicon) and `make dmg` -> `build/dist/LAS Recomp-<version>-macOS.dmg`.

### Windows

Requirements: Windows 10+ x86-64, a CPU with AVX2 and a GPU with Vulkan 1.3. More detail in
[docs/BUILD-windows.md](docs/BUILD-windows.md). Windows on ARM (experimental) builds with the same setup script; see
that page.

1. One-time setup, in PowerShell from the repo root: `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File tools\setup_windows.ps1`.
   It installs MSYS2 (UCRT64: clang, make, SDL3, FFmpeg, Vulkan, shaderc), Python 3.12 for the tools and the
   randomizer (`third_party\LAS-Randomizer\venv`) and switches the clone to LF line endings.
2. Build, from an MSYS2 UCRT64 shell (or Git Bash with `export PATH="/c/msys64/ucrt64/bin:/c/msys64/usr/bin:$PATH"`):
   `make -j` -> `build/lasrecomp.exe`. Set up your game files (above), then `make gen` and `make -j` again.
3. Run: `./build/lasrecomp.exe extracted`, from a shell with `C:\msys64\ucrt64\bin` on PATH (for the DLLs).
4. Package: `make deps-windows` (once: LGPL FFmpeg), `make rando-helper RANDO_PY="<path to python.org Python 3.12>"`
   (MSYS2's Python has no oead wheel), then `make dist` -> `build/dist/LAS Recomp-<version>-windows.zip`.
source_text.general:
## Status

This is a beta release. That means bugs are likely, crashes could occur, randomizer seeds could possibly be unsolvable (dungeon room shuffle modes are especially experimental at this point) and some graphics issues remain (especially in wide and ultrawide aspect ratios). This is a work in progress, hence the beta designation. To report a bug or a possible randomizer logic issue, open a [GitHub issue](https://github.com/peiikai/LASRecomp/issues) - see [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md#reporting-bugs) for what to include.

### Known issues

Known issues and their status are on the [GitHub issues page](https://github.com/peiikai/LASRecomp/issues).

## What you need

- Windows 10 / 11 (x64), a 64-bit CPU - AVX2 (Intel Haswell / AMD Zen or newer) recommended; older CPUs without AVX2
  (Intel Sandy / Ivy Bridge and earlier) are supported but slower - a GPU with Vulkan 1.3 and an up-to-date driver

source_text.installation: ## Install 1. Download the latest `...-windows.zip` from [Releases](../../releases) and extract it anywhere you own (for example `D:\Games`, **not** Program Files). Start `SuperOdysseyRecomp.exe`. It isn't code-signed: if SmartScreen says "Windows protected your PC", choose *More info*, then *Run anyway*. 2. The installer asks for: 1. **Your game**: the folder that holds the extracted **`exefs`** and **`romfs`** folders of your own Super Mario Odyssey - version **1.0.0**, or **1.4.1** with the update already applied (its full `romfs`, not only the update's). `exefs` holds `main`, `main.npdm` and `sdk`; `romfs` holds folders such as `StageData` and `SystemData`. 2. **Install the game to**: where the game data, saves and shaders go (about 12 GB). 3. Press **Install**. It copies the game data, recompiles the game code for your PC (a few minutes) and compiles every shader (several minutes, once). 4. Press **Play**. Every start then shows the start screen: **Play** (already selected: A, Enter or Start), **Settings** and **Exit**. Untick *Show this screen at every start* to go straight to the game.
source_text.build:
## Building from source

Needs MSYS2 (UCRT64: clang, SDL3, FFmpeg, shaderc, Python) - `tools\setup_windows.ps1` installs them. See
[docs/BUILD-windows.md](docs/BUILD-windows.md).

1. Put your extracted game folders into `extracted\` (`extracted\exefs\`, `extracted\romfs\`), or start the built
   program and let its installer copy them there.
2. From an MSYS2 UCRT64 shell in this folder:

       make gen        # recompile the game from extracted/exefs into generated/
       make -j16       # build/SuperOdysseyRecomp.exe and the game code, build/odyssey_game.dll
       make dlls       # copy SDL3 / FFmpeg / shaderc DLLs next to the exe

3. A release: `make deps-windows` (an LGPL-only FFmpeg), `make gen-helper`, `tools/fetch_zig.sh`, then `make dist`.
   The zip holds no game code.

# God Hand: Rearmed (かみて · おもてなし)

**God Hand for PS2. Recompiled, Refined, Rearmed.**

An unofficial, fan-made native PC port of Clover Studio's **God Hand** (PlayStation 2, 2006). The game's own code is
recompiled into a Windows program: no emulator running the show. It plays start to credits at a smooth 60, on any
screen, with as much or as little of our own nonsense as you want.

> [!WARNING]
> **Beta!** Plays from the first punch to the credits, but expect the odd bug. Found one? [Tell us](#found-a-bug).

> **No game files included!** Play your own damn copy! (USA, SLUS-21503; see [DISC_HASHES.md](DISC_HASHES.md)).

<!-- MEDIA: assets/readme/hero.gif — the hero shot: a fight at 60 FPS, widescreen -->

## Get It Running

1. Grab the latest `GHR-v….zip` from [Releases](https://github.com/God-Hand-Rearmed/God-Hand-Rearmed/releases).
2. Unzip it somewhere you can write to, **Not Program Files**!
    * The launcher updates the game in place and Windows won't let it write there.
3. Run **GHR.exe**. 
    * Windows SmartScreen may complain about an unknown publisher: **More info > Run anyway**.
4. Point the launcher at your disc image (.iso or .chd) once, and it checks it for you.
5. Pick a preset and hit "**Play**"! 
    * Beat thugs™, demons™, women™!

The first start compiles shaders for your GPU, so the screen may stay black before coming back. Patience, young ass-whooper.

## What's In It

<!-- MEDIA: assets/readme/launcher.png — the launcher -->

### God Hand - Gone Native!

Recompiled as a Windows program under Vulkan or DX11; PCSX2 as the renderer until later.

---

### You've Been Hit by, You've Been Struck by, My Smooth Visuals!

True 60FPS (fists punching swiftly) game logic, that by a thousand fixes was achieved. <!-- tag:Fps60 --> `Remastered+`

<!-- MEDIA: assets/readme/60fps.gif — 30 vs 60 side by side -->
---

### Wider Than Yo Momma's!

I'll kick up your goddamn Aspect Ratio, boy! 

Up to 32:9. With enemy behavior

![God Hand: Rearmed](assets/logo.png)

# God Hand: Rearmed (かみて · おもてなし)

**God Hand for PS2. Recompiled, Refined, Rearmed.**

An unofficial, fan-made native PC port of Clover Studio's **God Hand** (PlayStation 2, 2006). The game's own code is
recompiled into a Windows program: no emulator running the show. It plays start to credits at a smooth 60, on any
screen, with as much or as little of our own nonsense as you want.

> [!WARNING]
> **Beta!** Plays from the first punch to the credits, but expect the odd bug. Found one? [Tell us](#found-a-bug).

> **No game files included!** Play your own damn copy! (USA, SLUS-21503; see [DISC_HASHES.md](DISC_HASHES.md)).

<!-- MEDIA: assets/readme/hero.gif — the hero shot: a fight at 60 FPS, widescreen -->

## Get It Running

1. Grab the latest `GHR-v….zip` from [Releases](https://github.com/God-Hand-Rearmed/God-Hand-Rearmed/releases).
2. Unzip it somewhere you can write to, **Not Program Files**!
    * The launcher updates the game in place and Windows won't let it write there.
3. Run **GHR.exe**. 
    * Windows SmartScreen may complain about an unknown publisher: **More info > Run anyway**.
4. Point the launcher at your disc image (.iso or .chd) once, and it checks it for you.
5. Pick a preset and hit "**Play**"! 
    * Beat thugs™, demons™, women™!

The first start compiles shaders for your GPU, so the screen may stay black before coming back. Patience, young ass-whooper.

## What's In It

### God Hand - Gone Native!

Recompiled as a Windows program under Vulkan or DX11; PCSX2 as the renderer until later.

## Status and known issues

Early, but playable. Honest list:

- **Liberty City Stories:** the whole story has not been played through by hand. Verified so far: the opening, the first
  mission, driving, bikes, boats, a helicopter, saves, long soak runs. Real mouse, pad and visible windows were less
  tested. Full list: [docs/LCS.md](docs/LCS.md) "Known issues".
- **GTA Stories is a prototype:** the bridge is simple (straight, flat, plain coloured shapes, no traffic or pedestrians
  of its own); cutscenes keep each city's own hero; the far city can look a frame or two old and its colours are its
  game's own; crossing waits during cutscenes and while a city loads; the pause menu's own options are not synced
  between cities; a crash in either game closes the one-program mode.
- **Vice City behind a new card** has no story unless you provide a starter save (see above).
- **Platforms:** Windows is the main target; macOS (Apple Silicon) and Linux builds exist but get less testing.
  GTA Stories is Windows only for now.
- **Android:** see above.
- Report Vice City Stories PC problems that are not about GTA Stories or mods to
  [gothamor/gta-vcs-recomp](https://github.com/gothamor/gta-vcs-recomp); everything else to
  [this project's issues](https://github.com/batinium/gta-stories-recompiled/issues).

### Next (0.3.1)

Planned, not done yet:

- **Android, one app with both cities:** "GTA Stories Recompiled" as a single app. Today the both-cities mode on Android
  only works as a personal build with both games inside. Planned: import a both-cities code pack, like the single-game
  packs.
- **Android, both cities:** crossing between the cities (switched off for now), the cross-game cars and the Vic/Toni
  outfit packs on the phone.
- **PC launcher:** fetching the Android build's tools from the *Prepare for Android* button itself (today it names the
  setup command; the scripts in `tools/` offer the fetch).
- **GTA Stories:** the far city can freeze for a moment and then jump while the other game loads an area.
- **Mac:** GTA Stories (both cities) mode.

Prefer Haswell (Xeon E5 v3) or newer. - A page file on C: of 16384 MB initial and 24576 MB maximum if the game closes with `error 1450` (see [Troubleshooting](#troubleshooting)). - An SSD for the game and the shader cache. ## Download and play

You need a PC that meets the [system requirements](#system-requirements) and your copy of the game
(the folder with `eboot.bin`, `sce_module` and `sce_sys`).

**Steps**

1. Download `spartanport-windows.zip` from the
   [Releases page](https://github.com/FelipePrado0/SpartanPort/releases/latest).
2. Extract it to a folder of your choice, for example `C:\Games\spartanport-windows`. Do not run it from
   inside the zip.
3. Open **`SpartanPort.exe`**. If Windows shows "Windows protected your PC", click
   **More info**, then **Run anyway**: the program is not digitally signed.
4. Click **Choose the game folder**. It takes you to the **Game** page. Next to **Game folder**,
   click **Browse…** and select the folder with `eboot.bin`.
5. Back on **Home**, the cover art and "CUSA01623 · version 01.02" appear. Adjust **Quick
   settings** if you like: display mode, frame rate limit, render resolution and engine frame
   rate.
6. Click **Save** to keep pending changes, then **PLAY**. The first start prepares the game image;
   shader compilation can also affect startup and performance on later launches.

Patches and fixes are included and applied automatically: texture fix, skip videos with X and
120 FPS are on by default. Change the resolution and frame rate on **Home** or **Performance**.
The startup black-screen fix is always requested, even with an older saved patch selection;
patches apply only where their signatures match. A resolution patch replaces the texture fix.

**While playing**

- **Insert** on the keyboard, or **R3 + L2** on the controller, opens the port's menu: cheats,
  multipliers, image, performance and the performance overlay.
- Saved shaders load in the background. A small "Loading shader cache" note in the corner shows
  the progress.

**Next time**

- **`Play SpartanPort.exe`** starts the game straight away with your saved settings. You can
  make a desktop shortcut to it, or add it to Steam with **Add a Non-Steam Game**.
- Your saves, shader cache and log are in the `user` folder next to `SpartanPort.exe`. Keep
  that folder when you update.
- **Advanced → Check for updates** downloads and installs a new version. Your saves and settings
  are kept.

## Building from source

### Windows

Install [rustup](https://rustup.rs) (stable) and the Visual Studio Build Tools with the "Desktop
development with C++" workload; the launcher is built with cargo and needs no Python. The build
commands below use MSYS2 CLANG64; launcher commands marked PowerShell run on Windows.

1. Install MSYS2 (`winget install MSYS2.MSYS2`) and, in the **MSYS2 CLANG64** shell, the
   packages listed in [packaging/windows/README.md](https://github.com/FelipePrado0/SpartanPort/blob/main/packaging/windows/README.md).
2. Clone the repository with its submodules and build:

   ```bash
   git clone --recursive https://github.com/FelipePrado0/SpartanPort
   cd SpartanPort
   bash build.sh
   ```

3. Start the launcher (in PowerShell, in the project folder):

   ```powershell
   cd launcher-rust
   cargo run --release
   ```

4. On **Game**, choose the game folder and patches. Adjust **Graphics** and **Performance**,
   click **Save** for pending changes, then **PLAY**.

To play with the saved settings without opening the launcher's window (for a shortcut or Steam):

```powershell
cd launcher-rust
cargo build --release
.\target\release\spartanport-launcher.exe --play
```

Or without the launcher's settings, from a Git Bash or MSYS2 shell:

```bash
SPARTAN_GAME_DIR='D:\path\CUSA01623' bash run.sh
```

### Linux (Ubuntu 24.04)

For a fresh checkout, run the following in a Linux shell. The dependency script installs system
packages using sudo and selects GCC 14 as the default compiler. The launcher also needs
[rustup](https://rustup.rs) (stable). It is intended for Ubuntu 24.04; adapt dependencies for other
distributions. If already cloned, start in the repository and skip the first two commands.

```bash
git clone --recursive https://github.com/FelipePrado0/SpartanPort
cd SpartanPort
bash packaging/linux/ci-deps.sh
bash build.sh
cd launcher-rust
cargo run --release
```

To package an AppImage after the build:

```bash
bash packaging/linux/build.sh
./dist/spartanport-x86_64.AppImage
```

`packaging/linux/build.sh` builds the Rust launcher itself. Building on a newer distribution
can require a newer glibc; public release builds use Ubuntu 24.04. From the repository, use
`bash run.sh` for a direct start (it builds what is missing and runs the launcher's exe with
`--run`), with `SPARTAN_GAME_DIR=/path/to/CUSA01623` to name the game folder. For the saved
launcher settings without the window, run `launcher-rust/target/release/spartanport-launcher --play`.

## Download

The [**latest release**](https://github.com/HayatoG/iss_pc/releases/latest) is published when the maintainer chooses to bundle the accumulated changes. PRs build and test; approvals and merges do not trigger builds. On `main`, Linux and Windows build only through an authorized manual release run. Older ones stay under [Releases](https://github.com/HayatoG/iss_pc/releases) as history. See [how to publish](docs/RELEASES.md):

- **Linux x86-64** (glibc 2.39+: Ubuntu 24.04, Fedora 40, SteamOS 3.6 or newer): `infamous-linux-x86_64.tar.gz`
- **Windows 10 (1903 or newer) / 11, 64-bit**: `infamous-windows-x86_64.zip`

The packages open the Qt launcher by default; it adds about 55 MB to the download (measured on Linux; an estimate on Windows). If the new launcher does not open on your machine, use **inFAMOUS Second Son (classic)**, in the same folder.
source_text.build:
## Building from source

```bash
git clone --recursive https://github.com/HayatoG/iss_pc.git && cd iss_pc
cd port && ISS_LTO=OFF bash build.sh   # Linux: SDL3, Vulkan, FFmpeg, FreeType, Boost, fmt, Zydis, glslang
cd .. && ./infamous_launcher_qt.sh     # Qt launcher (needs PySide6); ./infamous_launcher.sh is the Tk one; ./run_infamous.sh from a terminal
```

A clone builds without profile-guided optimization (PGO): the profile (`port/pgo/*.gcda`) is not in the tree, and the release packages are built without it as well, so a local build and a package should perform alike. `ISS_PGO=generate` builds an instrumented binary that writes the profile while you play, and the next build uses it.

On Windows, the build runs in MSYS2 CLANG64 ([`port/packaging/windows/README.md`](port/packaging/windows/README.md)). The workflow [`.github/workflows/build.yml`](.github/workflows/build.yml) shows the full process on both platforms.

## What you need

- Your own copy of P.T. The port is built and tested with the US release, CUSA01127, as a dump folder from your console
  or a fake PKG made from that dump. The folder can have any name: the game recognises it by its files. Other releases,
  such as the European CUSA01114, are accepted the same way, but I have not seen their data myself; the game logs at its
  start what differs from the US data. A store PKG cannot be used: it is encrypted for the console that owns it, and nothing here
  decrypts it.
- Windows 10 or 11 (x64), Linux x86-64 with glibc 2.38 or newer (Ubuntu 24.04, Debian 13, Fedora 39, current Arch
  and SteamOS), or macOS 14 or newer on an Apple silicon or Intel Mac.
- A GPU and driver with Vulkan 1.3; on macOS the port brings MoltenVK, which runs Vulkan on Metal. The optional
  ray-traced shadows, ambient occlusion and reflections need a GPU with Vulkan ray queries (not on macOS). DLSS needs a
  GeForce RTX card. Available upscalers depend on the platform and renderer; see docs/upscaling.md. The settings page greys out what your machine
  cannot run and says why.
- A microphone for one part of the game, as on the PS4. If you have none, `key = J` under `[voice]` in `pt.ini` lets a
  key stand in for the spoken word.
source_text.installation:
## Installing

Download the installer from the Releases page: `P.T.PC.Port.Setup.exe` on Windows, the Linux setup binary on Linux.
Point it at your dump folder or fake PKG and at a destination folder (the default on Windows is
`%LocalAppData%\Programs\P.T. PC Port`). It copies the three game archives it needs (`chunk1.psarc`,
`texture.qar`, `pathid_list_ps4.bin`) next to the port and makes a shortcut if you want one. The eboot, modules and
system files are not used.

Linux: `chmod +x` the setup and run it from a terminal. The game needs only glibc and the system's Vulkan driver. On a Steam Deck
install from desktop mode and add `pt` as a non-Steam game; it runs on SteamOS as it is.

macOS: download `P.T.PC.Port-macOS-arm64.zip` (M1 and later) or `P.T.PC.Port-macOS-x64.zip` (Intel), unzip `P.T. PC Port.app`,
open it once and allow it under System Settings > Privacy & Security (it is not signed with a Developer ID), then pick your
dump folder when it asks. A fake PKG has to be extracted on Windows or Linux first. Intel Macs need a GPU that MoltenVK can
run the renderer on; the port was written without a Mac at hand and the Intel app has not been run on one yet. More in
docs/macos.md.

Windows and Linux releases include installers and portable ZIPs. To update an existing installation, use the game's update
button or run the new installer over it. Your game archives, settings, saves and mods stay.

On Windows and Linux, settings, saves, logs and cache live in `data/` beside the executable. The game migrates
existing user data without overwriting newer files. On macOS, these stay in `~/Library/Application Support/pt-port/pt/`.
The game checks GitHub Releases for a newer version at startup; `[network] check_updates = 0` disables that check.

Thanks to ahm3texe for the Apple silicon port, totsu0jv for Czech translation, and yewhochen for the Linux library-loading
and startup-focus fixes.

### Antivirus warnings

Some antivirus programs flag the installer or `pt.exe`. These are false positives. The files are not code signed (a
certificate costs more every year than this free project makes), and an installer that unpacks programs and starts one
of them is exactly what heuristic scanners watch for. On VirusTotal the release files are flagged by 1 to 3 engines out
of about 70. Every line of the port is in this repository, so you can read it or build it yourself (see Building from
source). If your antivirus stops the installer, save it to a folder first instead of opening it from the browser, or use
the portable ZIP.
source_text.build:
## Building from source

Windows: Visual Studio 2022 Build Tools, LLVM (clang-cl), the Vulkan SDK, CMake 3.28 and Ninja. Then

    tools\build_pt.bat release

gives `build\release\pt.exe`. CMake fetches the dependencies (SDL3, zlib, volk, VMA, glm, Dear ImGui, stb, Lua 5.1,
libogg, libvorbis, whisper.cpp and Google libsbc) and downloads the Whisper and Silero models and the upscaler SDK files, each checked by
SHA-256. Windows release builds require the upscaler SDKs and stop if required downloads fail. `python
tools\package.py` turns the build into the portable folder and zip.

Linux: `cmake -G Ninja -B build/linux -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo && cmake --build build/linux --target pt`.
GCC 13 or clang 17, the Vulkan headers and `glslc`. Linux includes DLSS and FSR 3.1; XeSS and DLSS Frame Generation are Windows-only.
`tools/linux/` has the cross build I use from Windows. More in docs/linux.md.

macOS (Apple silicon or Intel, built for the CPU it runs on): the command line tools, then `brew install cmake ninja shaderc
vulkan-headers vulkan-loader` and `cmake -G Ninja -B build/macos -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=RelWithDebInfo && cmake --build
build/macos --target pt`. `python3 tools/macos/make_app.py` makes the app bundle and its zip. The upscalers and the VR mode
are left out there too, and MoltenVK has no ray queries. More in docs/macos.md.

The unit tests are CMake targets (`pt_tests`, `pt_mods_test` and the others in CMakeLists.txt). `python
tools/walkthrough.py --exe build/release/pt.exe --game <folder>` plays the whole game without a window through the
scripted routes in `tests/walkthrough/` and checks the log; it is how I make sure a change did not break a loop.

The installer is `installer/`: a native C++ setup (`pt_setup`, built when a payload exists) and a small LGPL extraction
helper in C# that reads fake PKGs with LibOrbisPkg. docs/installer.md describes how it decides what it accepts.

Other docs: docs/upscaling.md, docs/vr.md, docs/updates.md, and the file format notes in docs/formats/ that came out of
reverse engineering the game data, with the tools in tools/ that read those formats.

# P.T. for PC **A native PC port of P.T., the 2014 PS4 teaser by Kojima Productions. Windows, Linux and macOS.** ![Lisa in the hallway](docs/media/lisa.gif)
> [!IMPORTANT] > **This port is made by one person in their spare time.** If it gave you a good scare, please consider supporting it on [**Patreon**](https://www.patreon.com/loreanxavier). It pays for the testing hardware and keeps the updates coming. > [!NOTE] > **Bug reports:** I've closed GitHub Issues because of ongoing spam attacks. Please join the [Discord server](https://discord.gg/3vKwUf2eTb) to report bugs. This is a native PC port of P.T., the 2014 PS4 teaser by Kojima Productions. It is not an emulator. The game logic was rebuilt in C++ from the original's behaviour, with Vulkan and DirectX 12 renderers; every level, model, texture, sound, script and cutscene is read at run time from your own copy of the PS4 game. There is no game data in this repository and none in the installer. The port runs on its own engine, Hallway Engine. I made this in my spare time, with AI tools (see AI Disclosure at the end), because P.T. deserved to keep existing somewhere other than on console

source_text.installation:
## Download and play

Nothing of the game is included in the release. You need your own retail Xbox 360 copy of Gears of War 2 (title ID `4D53082D`): a disc image (`.iso`) of it, or a folder that has `default.xex` and the `GearGame` folder, which you can still make by extracting your ISO with [xdvdfs](https://github.com/antangelo/xdvdfs):

```text
xdvdfs unpack "Gears of War 2.iso" C:\Games\GoW2
```

The port was recompiled from the US retail disc (its default.xex); other releases such as the European disc are untested and can crash, and the log says at start which one you have (`XEX default.xex ...`).

Do not pirate the game.

### PC

Requirements: Windows 10/11 x64 and a DirectX 12 GPU, or a Vulkan GPU for the experimental Vulkan option (developed on an AMD Radeon RX 7800 XT).

1. Download `gow2-recomp-<version>-win64.zip` from the [latest release](https://github.com/santiquiroz/gears-of-war-2-pc-port/releases/latest) (the `.apk` is the Android build).
2. Unzip it anywhere and run `gow2.exe`. The exe is not signed, so Windows may show "Windows protected your PC": choose **More info**, then **Run anyway**.
3. The first launch asks for your `.iso`, or for `default.xex` in an extracted game folder (one that also has `GearGame`), and remembers the game folder in `gow2_game_path.txt` next to the exe. With an `.iso` it extracts it once into a `game` folder next to `gow2.exe`, which needs about 8 GB free on that drive; you can delete the `.iso` afterwards if you want. To pick another folder later, delete `gow2_game_path.txt`.

It does not ask when the game folder is inside the exe's folder or right next to it, when the exe's folder is inside the game folder, or when you pass the folder yourself (`--game_data_root` also takes the .iso):

```text
gow2.exe --game_data_root="C:\Games\GoW2"
```

The first time you play System Link co-op, Windows asks whether `gow2.exe` may use the network: allow it, or the other players will not find your game.

The first start, and the first start after an update that changes the graphics, compiles the shaders again: the window can sit on the title screen for a few minutes and Windows may call it "Not responding", and the first level takes a little longer to load. Leave it running; later starts use the saved shaders.

### Linux and SteamOS (experimental)

A native Linux build for Steam Deck, Legion Go with SteamOS and desktop distributions with Vulkan. It needs the extracted game folder (it cannot extract an `.iso` itself; use xdvdfs or copy the folder the Windows build made).

1. Download `gow2-recomp-<version>-linux-x86_64.tar.gz` from the [latest release](https://github.com/santiquiroz/gears-of-war-2-pc-port/releases/latest)

- [x] Native renderer (0.3.0; draws taken from the game's Direct3D calls since 0.3.4): render targets are host surfaces and resolves write textures directly instead of emulating the Xbox 360 EDRAM. On by default only on Android since 0.3.15 (before: AMD, NVIDIA since 0.3.8, and Android); on PC it is a Graphics > Renderer > Native choice, since it smears on some cards (issue #26) (`gow2_native_renderer`)

- [x] Graphics API on PC: Direct3D 12 (default) or Vulkan, experimental (PC Options > Graphics > Graphics API, `gpu_backend`, 0.3.8). On Vulkan the temporal upscalers are not available; FSR 1 and CAS are
- [x] Install from your own `.iso` on PC (0.3.6) and on Android (0.2.6)

## Getting started

### What you need

These files, from your own console or discs. The first start asks for them in this order.

1. **The game**, World release (`544307D5`), in any one of these forms:
   - a disc image: `*.iso`
   - the Games on Demand package: the file in `544307D5/00007000` (named like
     `C1200E9B558D04454FA6`), with its `.data` folder next to it
   - an extracted copy: the folder with `default.xex` and the `.ng2` archives
2. **Title Update 3** (required): `TU_1A461UL_000000G000000.00000000000O4`, or the `default.xexp`
   taken from it. On a console it is in `Content/0000000000000000/544307D5/000B0000`. The port is
   built for this update and checks it; the Japanese release's Title Update 3 is refused.
3. **The DLC** (optional): the console's `544307D5/00000002` folder, with Mission Mode and the
   costume packs. It can also be added later, in the game folder's `dlc` folder.

And a 64-bit PC with SSE4.2 (any from about 2009 on) and a GPU with Vulkan 1.3 drivers.

The first start after installing takes longer to load: the render pipelines are made then and
kept, and later starts are quicker.

### Linux and Steam Deck

1. Download `NinjaGaiden2-x86_64.AppImage` from the releases page and make it executable
   (`chmod +x`, or Properties → Allow executing).
2. Run it. On the first start it asks whether to keep everything next to the AppImage (portable
   mode, below), then for your copy of the game, Title Update 3 and, if you have it, the DLC folder. A disc image or package is copied once into the data folder (below).
   More DLC can go in the game folder's `dlc` folder later; it is installed on the next start.
3. On a Steam Deck, add the AppImage to Steam (Add a Non-Steam Game) to play it in Game Mode, and
   choose 16:10 in RECOMP SETTINGS → Display.

Needs a 64-bit Linux with glibc 2.35 or newer (SteamOS, Ubuntu 22.04+, Debian 12, Fedora 36+),
and Python 3. The first-start windows use `kdialog` (SteamOS and KDE desktops), or `qarma` or
`zenity` where kdialog isn't installed (GNOME, Cinnamon, Xfce...). With none of them, start the
AppImage from a terminal and it asks there. An extracted copy of the game next to the AppImage
(`default.xex` beside it, or in a `game_files` or `game` folder there) is used without asking, as
is `NG2_GAME_DIR`; Title Update 3's `default.xexp` goes next to `default.xex` and DLC in its `dlc`
folder.

### Windows

1. Download `NinjaGaiden2-windows-x64.zip` from the releases page and extract it anywhere.
2. Run `ng2.exe`. The first time it asks about portable mode (below), then for the game, Title Update 3 and the DLC as on Linux; a
   disc image or package is copied into `%LOCALAPPDATA%\NinjaGaiden2\game`.

## Building from source

The build needs the game's code, so it starts from your own disc image. Requirements: clang 20+,
CMake 3.25+, Ninja, Python 3, the Vulkan headers and loader, FFmpeg (libavformat, libavcodec,
libswresample, libswscale).

1. Clone with its submodules: the ReXGlue SDK, XenosRecomp (the shader translator) and plume (the
   Vulkan layer of Unleashed Recompiled), each a fork with this port's changes on its `ng2` branch
   ([rexglue-sdk](https://github.com/gamboozino/rexglue-sdk),
   [XenosRecomp](https://github.com/gamboozino/XenosRecomp),
   [plume](https://github.com/gamboozino/plume)). Then build and install the SDK:

       git clone --recursive https://github.com/gamboozino/ng2recomp
       cd ng2recomp/thirdparty/rexglue-sdk
       cmake --preset linux-amd64
       cmake --build out/build/linux-amd64 --config Release --target install
       cd ../..

   (In a clone made without `--recursive`: `git submodule update --init --recursive`.)

2. Extract the disc (or the Games on Demand package) into `game_files/` and put Title Update 3's
   `default.xexp` next to `default.xex` (see [docs/title-update.md](docs/title-update.md)):

       python3 tools/xdvdfs_extract.py "Ninja Gaiden II (World).iso" game_files
       python3 tools/stfs_extract.py TU_1A461UL_000000G000000.00000000000O4 default.xexp game_files/default.xexp

3. Build. This generates about 560 MB of C++ from the game's code and translates its shaders
   (see [docs/shaders.md](docs/shaders.md)):

       cmake --preset linux-amd64-release
       cmake --build out/build/linux-amd64-release

4. Run it:

       out/build/linux-amd64-release/ng2 --game_data_root=game_files

The AppImage, `packaging/appimage/build.sh`, builds the SDK and the game in an Ubuntu 22.04
container (Docker; `packaging/appimage/Dockerfile`; it also needs rsync,
zsync (`zsyncmake`, for the `.zsync` updaters use) and
[appimagetool](https://github.com/AppImage/appimagetool) on the PATH, or `APPIMAGETOOL=<path>`), so it needs only glibc 2.35 and runs on
SteamOS and other current distributions. It bundles a small FFmpeg with the movies' codecs and
writes `out/appimage/NinjaGaiden2-x86_64.AppImage`. `packaging/appimage/build-local.sh` packs
the native build instead, quicker but only for the machine that built it.

The Windows build is cross-compiled from Linux after the native one: `packaging/windows/build.sh`
(clang and lld against Microsoft's C runtime and Windows SDK from
[xwin](https://github.com/Jake-Shadle/xwin), `xwin --accept-license splat --output ~/.xwin`). It builds the SDK for Windows, fetches
FFmpeg's Windows build, and packs `out/windows/NinjaGaiden2-windows-x64.zip`.

## Known issues

- Some cutscenes may have slight audio delays.
- Overlays and frame limiters that hook the game's presents (MSI Afterburner with RivaTuner, and the
  like) can upset frame pacing: if the game looks choppy at a steady 60 fps, close them completely
  (not only minimized) and try again.
- Frame Interpolation (experimental): some objects or effects can flicker or judder. It is meant for
  displays above 60 Hz and adds a little input latency. It is off in cutscenes for now, which play at
  the game's own rate, until the problems it causes there are solved. Please report any issues with it.
- Tested on a Linux desktop, the Steam Deck, under Proton and in a Windows 11 virtual machine; reports
  from other systems, and from real Windows PCs especially, are welcome.

When reporting a graphics glitch, pressing **F7** while it is on screen records the next frames'
drawing to `~/ng2-trace-<n>` (Linux) or `C:\Users\<you>\ng2-trace-<n>` (Windows): attach that
folder, zipped. For a crash or a freeze, attach the log (`ng2.log`, above).
