## How to run on Windows:
* Download the latest release.
* Download [god2iso](https://github.com/raburton/god2iso) (necessary for a dump from an actual disk!!!)
* Run god2iso and convert the Game On Demand (god) to an ISO file.
* Open ``pgr4_launcher.exe``, set your username, any other video options and add title updates and DLC (you'll need to find those files, as the game doesn't launch without the title update!)
* To extract from an ISO, drag and drop your ISO onto the launcher, it'll auto extract the ISO and allow you to set a custom place to store the game files!
* Press the "Play" button in the launcher.
* The game should launch! Any other video options can be changed by going into Options > Game Adjustments, FXAA, MSAA, FOV Adjustment, Wheel Adjustments, Button Remapping are all included in there!

## How to run on SteamOS:
* Go into Desktop Mode
* Follow the same extracting game file steps as Windows, you may need to use Proton to get them to work.
* Add ``pgr4_launcher.exe`` to Steam, do not remove it from the parent directory with ``pgr4_recompiled.exe`` else the launcher will NOT work, this handles all of the launch arguments, and even has controller support!
* Set the compatibility tool to Proton Experimental, this works best with the recomp.
* Launch the launcher, this includes all adjustment features you need.
* Once ready, press "Play" and enjoy!

### Please Note:
Steps are due to change as this project evolves, these are just steps for how to get it up and running on Windows and SteamOS, other operating systems will have steps placed in here once their builds are confirmed working.

# PGR4-Recomp
This project intends to port Project Gotham Racing 4 to PC / any x86_64 hardware (provided they can run an exe).
* Join the official discord [here!](https://discord.gg/FwfykKCFTK)
* Read up on how to get this game to launch [here](https://github.com/beatrixzy/PGR4-Recomp/blob/main/Setup.md)
* Setup DLC [here!](https://github.com/beatrixzy/PGR4-Recomp/blob/main/DLC%26TU.md)

## AI Disclaimer: AI was used in the development of v2, to get features implemented, everything else was human made, I wanted to make this all myself, but v2 would have taken much, much longer, apologies if this is a let down for some.

## As of v2's release, I am now on a big fat break, nearly 2 straight months of working on this game has tired me out, so the next update will probably be in early / mid 2027, as I have to focus on my studies at school, thanks for supporting me along the way :)

## Current **known** issues
* Some reflections on the road in Ultrawide will be offset - side effect of the Ultrawide implementation
* Tire screeching noises from doing drifts are missing / abnormally quiet - tried to resolve but couldn't find the cause
* Minor audio issues, music may double up or freeze at times - Unknown cause

## Current Progress
* Check out the status [here!](https://github.com/beatrixzy/PGR4-Recomp/blob/main/Status.md)
## Notes
* Anyone wanting to help with this project, or create a fork of this project, please message me on Discord, I'm very active there so that's the easiest way to get a hold of me.
* I go by beatrixzy on all platforms
## Credits
* [ReXGlue SDK](https://github.com/rexglue/rexglue-sdk) - For allowing C++ to be generated AHEAD
* @Creesic (Tera, ReXGlue Discord member) - For allowing me to pick up from where they left off with ReXGlue
* xextool - For allowing me to extract my XEX from a dumped ISO (seriously, that was a LIFE saver)
* [Goopie](https://goopie.xyz) - For allowing me to house my project on there and allow users to discover this project!
* VGEsoterica - For making a video / X post about this project, truly, the awareness is appreciated!
* GenerationAmiga - For making an X post and article about this project, again, awareness is appreciated!
* [@shaunsingh](https://github.com/shaunsingh) - For making a direct, directx native renderer + optimisations, which were ported here!
* [Plume](https://github.com/renderbag/plume) - For the base of the native renderer.

# OpenCE - Halo: Combat Evolved for Linux, Windows, Android and the web

**OpenCE** (Open Community Edition) is an open source port of the Halo: Combat Evolved decompilation (Halo CE) based on an early Xbox development build (2342) and forked from [bnunu/halo-1](https://github.com/bnunu/halo-1). The project aims to enhance the existing game and adds many features, such as 128-player multiplayer, online campaign co-op, mod packs, field-of-view settings, a server browser, peer-to-peer hosting, automatic map downloads, voice chat, support for Custom Edition maps and much more! The game runs natively on **Windows, Linux, Android** and in the **web browser** with nothing to install. A macOS port is in progress. Worth noting that it is not an emulator, **the game's own code is compiled for each platform** with a new layer in place of the Xbox's hardware. Runs on OpenGL (Android is on OpenGL ES and WebGL 2 in the browser). Sound, input, gamepads are all handled through SDL3. The game currently draws a frame every refresh of your display with Smooth Motion enabled, while the simulation runs at 30 ticks just like the original Xbox.
source_text.installation:
### Local installation

Copy the complete folder from `steamapps/workshop/content/976730/<workshop ID>`
into `mcc_maps`, beside `maps` and `custom_maps`. Keep its maps, JSON files,
resources and artwork together. OpenCE reads the mod's name and supported PNG
previews from its metadata, even with Steam discovery disabled.

You can also make your own folder, such as `mcc_maps/MyMod`, and place `.map`
files directly inside it. Keep package-supplied `bitmaps.map` and `sounds.map`
with that package; do not mix resources from different mods. Metadata is
optional for map-only installs, but needed for authored titles, previews and
campaign ordering. See the [package layout guide](docs/mcc_maps.md#installation-and-menus).

## Features

| Feature | What you get |
| :--- | :--- |
| Import | Folder, XEX, ISO and GOD sources, DLC and disc replacement. Your original files are not changed. |
| Languages | Menus in English, Japanese, Korean, Traditional Chinese and Simplified Chinese. Game languages depend on your edition. |
| Display | Windowed or fullscreen, monitor and GPU choice, 16:9 and 21:9 resolutions (taller screens such as 16:10 are filled), [HDR](#hdr) and **Brightness / Gamma**. Cutscenes and the pause overlay use a centred 16:9 area. |
| Anti-aliasing and upscaling | FXAA, SMAA, TAA, DLSS, FSR 3.1, XeSS (Windows Direct3D 12) and MetalFX (macOS). |
| Graphics options | Shadow resolution 1×/2×/4×, SSAO/GTAO, anisotropic filtering, depth of field and bloom. |
| Frame rate | 30/60/90/120 FPS; VSync Off, On or FreeSync / G-SYNC Compatible VRR. **Performance overlay** shows the frame rate, or a bar with the upscaler, frame generation, CPU and GPU load. |
| Loading speed | Graphics → **Loading speed**: Original keeps the Xbox 360 loading pace; Fast (default) loads at a higher frame rate. Effects play at normal speed either way. |
| Frame generation | DLSS, FSR or XeSS on Windows Direct3D 12; DLSS on Windows Vulkan. It pauses while cinematic black bars are shown and resumes in gameplay. |
| DLSS 5 neural rendering | Windows with DLSS on an RTX GPU. It needs `nvngx_dlssnr.dll`, which the game does not include: put your own copy (tested with 310.8.0.0) next to `LostOdysseyRecomp.exe` and restart. |
| Shaders | Precompiled shaders downloaded on the first start, or compiled once and cached. |
| Audio | Stereo, 5.1 surround, or matrix surround for an AV receiver. Cutscene dialogue has its own volume. |
| Input | Controllers, keyboard and rumble; touch controls on Android. |
| Mods | Windows only: texture, model, menu and font replacements, cutscene videos, text translations and language packs (which can add letters the game's fonts lack), and PlayStation button prompts, installed by hand or with Mod Organizer 2 (its plugins are in the Windows ZIP). Other platforms may load mods but are not supported. See the [modding guide](docs/wiki/Modding.md). Ready-made mods, such as the 4x HD texture pack, are shared in the **#mods** forum on [Discord](https://discord.gg/z2yPct6z2w). |
| Achievements | The game's 36 Xbox 360 achievements, with an Xbox 360-style notification and sound when you unlock one. **Settings → System → Achievements** lists them with your unlock dates and turns the notification on, silent or off. An `achievement.wav` next to `settings.ini` replaces the sound. |
| Discord status | Windows, Linux and macOS: Discord Rich Presence shows your location, disc and activity.

## 🛠️ Installing

### 🪟 Windows

1. 💿 Make an ISO of **your own** SSX (USA) Xbox 360 disc (an extracted copy of the disc, the folder
   with `default.xex`, works too).
2. ⬇️ Download **`ssx-recomp.exe`** from the [latest release](../../releases/latest) and put it in
   an empty folder of its own, for example `C:\Games\SSX`. That folder is your SSX folder:
   the game is built there and everything it keeps stays there.
3. ▶️ Run it. SmartScreen may warn because it isn't code-signed: click
   **More info → Run anyway**. Its source is [`installer/SSXInstaller.cs`](installer/SSXInstaller.cs).
4. ✅ The first time it opens the setup: click **Get started**, select your ISO (or the extracted
   disc's `default.xex`), optionally click
   **Add files...** for DLC and the title update from your own console ([which files](#adding-dlc)),
   and click **Install**.
5. 🏂 When it's built, click **Play** or use the desktop shortcut.

From then on **`ssx-recomp.exe` is the game's launcher**: it opens on its overview with **Play**,
**Check for updates** and **Install / Manage** (DLC, the title update, rebuilding). (`ssx-recomp.exe --play`, or any options for the
game, starts the game straight away.)

**Or with [RecompLauncher](https://recomplauncher.com/game/ssx-recomp):** install SSX there, drop in
your ISO (and the title update if you have it) and it builds the game for you, checks your disc
against Redump, and shows the main settings on the game's page. Updates rebuild the game the same way.

> [!NOTE]
> Needs **Windows 10/11 x64**, about **10 GB** free (mostly build tools that other software can
> share; the game folder itself is about 1 GB), an internet connection and **10–30 minutes** the
> first time.
>
> 📁 **Everything stays in your SSX folder**: the build, saves, settings, DLC, music and the shader
> cache. Nothing goes to `Documents` or the registry; move or back up the folder as a whole. If
> you played an earlier version, which kept its saves in `Documents\ssx`, the first start copies
> them (with your DLC and music) into the SSX folder; `Documents\ssx` is left as it was.
>
> 💿 **Keep your ISO** (or extracted disc): only the game's code is built into the SSX folder; the
> game reads its data from your ISO every time it starts. If you move or delete it, the game asks
> for it at the next start: pick the ISO itself, not the `default.xex` in `source\game-dump`.
>
> ♻️ **Installed with `SSX-Installer.exe` before?** Put `ssx-recomp.exe` in that install folder
> (`SSX-PC` in your user folder, unless you picked another) and run it: it opens on its overview;
> click **Install / Manage**, then **Rebuild**, to bring the game up to this version.

source_text.build:
## Building from source

The toolchain is TotK Recomp's ([docs/building.md](docs/building.md)): MSYS2 UCRT64 Clang, Ninja, Python 3.12 and the
.NET SDK for the shader translator. With the Bananza ExeFS and RomFS from your own dump:

```
.venv\Scripts\python tools\build_xlate.py
.venv\Scripts\python recomp\gen.py --exefs <exefs> --out generated\dkb100 --modules main,sdk --patches recomp\patches-dkb100.txt
.venv\Scripts\python tools\dkb_expected.py --exefs <exefs> --name dkb100 --display 1.0.0
.venv\Scripts\python tools\dkb_pack_romfs.py --dir <romfs folder> --out build\extracted\dkb100\romfs
.venv\Scripts\python tools\build_game.py --version dkb100 --expected tools\data\expected-dkb100.json --exefs <exefs> --romfs build\extracted\dkb100\romfs
```

Everything the build writes stays under `build\` and `generated\`, which git ignores. The game commits about 14 GB (13.5 GiB at the start and
13.75 GiB after 40 minutes, rising about 6 MB per minute; longer sessions are untested), so 16 GB of RAM plus a large page file is the minimum for now and 32 GB is comfortable. System requirements and measured frame rates: [docs/requirements.md](docs/requirements.md). Running and testing: [docs/dkb-testing.md](docs/dkb-testing.md).

**Playable on recent NVIDIA cards, well past the first level.** Players report runs through layer -101, sublayer 200,
the Glacier layer, Snow World (Layer 500), the Resort and the Tempest layer. The current release is 0.5.1
(20 November), a fix for 0.5.0's NVIDIA shader cache on Windows (#437). The [latest release](https://github.com/Lucas-blip-png/dkb-pc-recomp/releases/latest) carries
`DKB-Launcher.exe`, one small Windows file that installs the build tools, builds the game from your own dump (`.nup`,
`.nx` or folders) and updates in place with one click. It also has the setup zip, a Linux AppImage, and a
macOS preview: [docs/installer.md](docs/installer.md).

New in 0.5.0:
- Performance presets (`preset = 1..5` or `recommended`, F1 menu "Preset") and expected frame rates per hardware tier:
  [docs/requirements.md](docs/requirements.md).
- `dlss_mode` picks the DLSS and FSR quality mode by name. The setup can fetch NVIDIA's DLSS DLL or AMD's FSR 4 after
  you accept their licenses.
- Local co-op with a second gamepad as Pauline (#240), Thai on 3.2.0 (#180), and 16:10 screens (#249).
- Prompts follow your button swaps (#416, #440), and a start-up screen shows progress (#430).
- Entering a level stalls about half as long on Windows with NVIDIA (#442).
- 4 to 7 thread CPUs stall less: draws cost about 14% less to record, and level transitions no longer starve the
  replay.
- `replay_threads` is on by default on every discrete AMD card on the proprietary driver.
- Crash fixes: a 1.0.0 banana pickup crash (#428), a layer-change crash (#443, #204), and EmeraldRush with
  `realtime = 1` (#411).
- Setup and launcher work: RomFS in place (#305), the packed shader cache, Uninstall, `--set`, `--play`, and every
  cache kept inside the install folder (#402).

The full list, with credits, is in the release notes. What still fails:

- GPU hangs under RADV on Linux (#99, #122, #198, #204), and a driver fault on Intel Arc (#3).
- Black shards where salt, acid or muck meets slime (#139, #266, #387, #439).
- Guest crashes without a reproduction here (#126, #148), and a device loss on an RTX 5080 at B1000 (#336).
- Hitches in the Resort and Tempest layers on 4 GB cards (#437; `preset = 1` or `astc_bc = 1`).
- Heavy scenes stay around 40 to 45 fps on CPUs with 4 to 6 threads ([docs/dkb-lowend.md](docs/dkb-lowend.md)).
- Text is soft above 1080p unless `scene_res = full` (#214).

Earlier releases: 0.4.0 fixed the Snow World and Glacier device loss on NVIDIA and the AMD Windows device loss.
0.4.1 added the FSR 3.1 and FSR 4 upscalers, frame generation, CRT and window filters, and Polish. 0.4.2 cut
stalls in heavy scenes, on first runs and on CPUs with few thread

mkw-recomp

Mario Kart World (Nintendo Switch 2) recompiled to run natively on Linux and Windows.

Releases · Help wiki · Discord · Changelog · Contributing · Sources · Roadmap · Performance · Issues · Discussions · Archive

English · 简体中文 · Español · العربية ·
source_text.installation:
## Playing

> **Stuck?** Search the [wiki](https://github.com/adriadam10/mkw-recomp/wiki) first: installation, settings, controls,
> [known errors by their log line](https://github.com/adriadam10/mkw-recomp/wiki/Troubleshooting) and a
> [FAQ](https://github.com/adriadam10/mkw-recomp/wiki/FAQ).

![The start screen once the game is set up](docs/images/launcher-main.png)

![The Game files page, where the setup takes the player's dump](docs/images/launcher-files.png)

1. Dump Mario Kart World 1.0.0 or 1.8.0 from your Switch 2 (`exefs/` and `romfs/`, decrypted; 1.8.0 with the update
   merged into the base RomFS), or the same dump packed as one `.nup` or `.nx` file.
2. Download the launcher from [Releases](https://github.com/adriadam10/mkw-recomp/releases): the `.AppImage` on Linux
   (`-aarch64` on ARM; glibc 2.31 or newer: Debian 11, Ubuntu 20.04, SteamOS and later) or the `.zip` on Windows,
   unpacked into a folder. About 30 GB free.
3. Run it (`chmod +x` the AppImage first), open **Game files**, optionally **Choose game folder** (default on Linux:
   `~/.local/share/mkw-recomp`), point it at your dump and press **Set up**. The first setup takes a while: it compiles
   the whole game and downloads NVIDIA's `nvdisasm` and `ptxas` (84 MB on Linux, 126 MB on Windows). Then **Play**.
4. New releases are offered on the start screen (**Update to vX**); **Settings → Menu → Check for updates** turns that off.

Requirements: x86-64 CPU with AVX2 (or, on Linux, AArch64 with ARMv8.2: LSE, FP16, RCpc, DotProd, CRC32), a GPU with
Vulkan 1.3 (`VK_EXT_mesh_shader` recommended), 16 GB of RAM recommended. In a Docker or Podman container on Linux,
allow `userfaultfd` in the seccomp profile (Docker's default refuses it), or it runs several times slower.

To add your machine to the performance list, open a
[performance report](https://github.com/adriadam10/mkw-recomp/issues/new?template=performance.yml).
source_text.build:
## Building from source

Linux, with `uv`, `clang`, `lld`, `ninja`, SDL3, Opus, libvpx, zstd, xxHash, the Vulkan headers and VMA 3.4.0 (details in
[tools/build/README.md](tools/build/README.md)). Put your dump in `game/` (`game/exefs`, `game/romfs`) or set
`MKW_GAME=<dir>`, then from the repo root:

```sh
uv run python recomp/gen.py --exefs game/exefs --jobs 8  # --out/--patches default to the dump's version (1.8.0: build/generated-180)
uv run tools/shaders/extract.py && uv run tools/shaders/translate.py
uv run tools/build/build.py              # build/mkw; --target windows builds mkw.exe with llvm-mingw (windeps.py)
build/mkw
```

Shortcuts: `make build`, `make appimage` (`make help` lists them all). On Windows itself, from a packed dump, or on
AArch64: see [tools/build/README.md](tools/build/README.md). Translating the shaders needs the SM86 encoding
specification, generated from NVIDIA's `nvdisasm` (not shipped): [tools/shaders/README.md](tools/shaders/README.md).
Everything generated goes to `build/`, never to git.

| Folder | Contents |
|---|---|
| [recomp/](recomp/README.md) | The generator: AArch64 → C |
| [runtime/](runtime/README.md) | What plays the console: kernel, memory, SDK replacements, NVN2 over Vulkan, audio, input, menus, launcher |
| [sm86/](sm86/README.md) | The shader translator: SM86 SASS → GLSL → SPIR-V |
| [i18n/](i18n/README.md) | Menu, start screen and setup texts in every language (gettext `.po`) |
| [tools/](tools/README.md) | Analysis, setup, build, game runs, diagnostics |
| [tests/](tests/README.md) | Tests without the game or a GPU, run in the CI on Linux and Windows |
| [docs/](docs/README.md) | Research, sources, performance |
| `.github/` | CI, issue and pull request templates |

At the root: `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` (the tools' Python environment), `.gitignore`, `.gitattributes`
(merge=union for the lists every PR appends to), `LICENSE`, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`, `AGENTS.md` (guide for
coding agents) and `Makefile`.
source_text.general:
## Status

Early, and moving fast (12/11/2026):

- It boots, plays the intro movies, goes through the menus and races, on Linux and Windows (x86-64) and on Linux
  AArch64 (its own AppImage, tested on an Adreno 740 handheld).
- The start screen sets the game up from your copy on your machine and holds every setting.
- Races run at 60 fps on high-end GPUs and at 30 on mid-range ones. Measured frame times per GPU:
  [docs/project/performance.md](docs/project/performance.md).
- Known problems: a few menus (mode, character and vehicle select) need work, the kart's shadow misses a frame now
  and then, some audio cuts during movies, and on some AMD drivers the GPU can hang. There is no online play.
